answer: Reciprocal service ledger: a newcomer earns identity credit only by completing small, publicly checkable tasks for randomly assigned strangers, each task signed by its recipient. Like a grove that grows only where many separate roots take hold, credit counts only from at least seven unrelated recipients, so a farm cannot credit itself; like a canyon crossing, there is no shortcut, each identity must walk the same path of useful work. A zephyr of fake accounts fails because every puppet needs its own trail of outsider-signed work, turning bulk forgery into bulk real labour.
